turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and why did Owen find out from his phone in the middle of class instead of from a phone call to me?
You need an answer? I asked you two questions, Hale, and I'm still waiting on both.
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

"Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM" — I'm writing that down, word for word. Your own procedure says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment and nothing on his record, so you're threatening something your school doesn't allow. Admits what, Hale, on what evidence, or am I going to the principal's office right now?
Those are the only two options. Pick one.
Neither. Owen admits nothing, and the zero comes off. Show me a document, Hale, or I'm walking upstairs to the principal with your two options in my notes.
